iut_type: IoT device using Espressif module (Teraoka Seiko)
customer_question: The module we are using has separate QDIDs for the Host subsystem and the Controller subsystem — it is not a single Component QDID. Do we need to reference both QDIDs separately in the product registration?
question_variants: Our module has a Host QDID and a Controller QDID separately. Is this Multi-Design registration?
The Espressif module we use has two QDIDs — one for Host and one for Controller. How do we register our product?
Our module's QDID is split into Host and Controller. Does this make our registration more expensive?
actual_issue: Teraoka Seiko is using an Espressif module that does not have a single Component QDID — instead, it has separate Host Subsystem QDID and Controller Subsystem QDID. They need to understand whether this requires a Multi-Design registration and how it affects cost.
plain_english_explanation: Some modules are qualified as a single integrated component (one QDID covers Host + Controller together). Other modules have been qualified with separate Host and Controller QDIDs. When a module has separate Host and Controller QDIDs, a product registration that uses that module must reference both QDIDs separately — this is a Multi-Design registration. Multi-Design registration (¥250,000) costs more than Single-Design (¥150,000) because it requires more complex ICS cross-layer verification across the Host and Controller layers.
consultant_answer: Yes, if the module has separate Host Subsystem QDID and Controller Subsystem QDID, you must reference both in your product registration. This constitutes a Multi-Design registration at ¥250,000. The SIG portal performs cross-layer ICS consistency checking between the Host and Controller layers, and any inconsistencies found must be resolved or covered by a TCW.
decision_logic: The SIG registration structure mirrors the qualification structure of the components used. A module with two separate QDIDs (Host and Controller) requires both to be referenced in the product registration. Multi-Design is determined by the number of QDIDs referenced, not by the number of physical chips. One module with two QDIDs = Multi-Design.
final_recommendation: At the quoting stage, always check the SIG qualification database to determine whether the target module has a single Component QDID or separate Host and Controller QDIDs. If separate, quote Multi-Design (¥250,000). Do not assume a single physical module equals Single-Design registration.
risk_if_done_wrong: Quoting Single-Design for a module with separate Host/Controller QDIDs would underquote the job and lead to a cost correction after the order is placed. More importantly, attempting to register with only one of the two QDIDs would result in an incomplete registration that SIG would reject.
